cards.definition: The list of things you have to do and when; also to arrange a time.
cards.example:
- My schedule is full until the fifteenth.
Minha agenda está cheia até o dia quinze.
cards.note: EUA: “SKÉ-jul”. Reino Unido: “SHÉ-dyul”. Também é verbo: to schedule a reunião.

cards.definition: A fixed time to meet someone, often a doctor or a client.
cards.example:
- I have an appointment with the dentist at four.
Tenho uma consulta com o dentista às quatro.
cards.note: Com médico, dentista ou cliente: appointment. Com colegas: meeting.

cards.definition: Extra time before something happens; a hold-up.
cards.example:
- There is a two-day delay in the delivery.
Tem um atraso de dois dias na entrega.
cards.note: Coisa atrasada é delayed; pessoa atrasada é late. Nunca “I am delayed”.

cards.example:
- We have a weekly call every Monday.
Temos uma reunião semanal toda segunda.
cards.note: A família toda: daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, yearly.

cards.example:
- I check my email twice a day.
Eu checo meu e-mail duas vezes por dia.
cards.note: Uma vez = once; duas = twice; de três em diante = three times.

cards.definition: Expected or required by a certain date.
cards.example:
- The report is due on Friday.
O relatório tem prazo até sexta.
cards.note: Be due = ter prazo. Já passou do prazo? overdue.

cards.definition: A polite question to agree on a time.
cards.example:
- I'm free after three. What time works for you?
Estou livre depois das três. Que horário funciona para você?
cards.note: Mais natural que “what time can you”. A resposta usa o mesmo verbo: Three works for me.

cards.translation: vamos passar para / vamos remarcar para
cards.definition: Used to suggest changing something to another day or time.
cards.example:
- Let's move it to Thursday morning, then.
Então vamos passar para quinta de manhã.
cards.note: O jeito leve de adiar. Formal: postpone. Adiantar: move it up.

cards.definition: Facts and numbers used to make decisions.
cards.example:
- I need more data before the meeting.
Preciso de mais dados antes da reunião.
cards.note: “Data” (o dia) é date! Data = números e informações.

cards.definition: An agreement where each side gives up something.
cards.example:
- Nobody was happy, so we found a compromise.
Ninguém ficou feliz, então achamos um meio-termo.
cards.note: “Compromisso” é appointment ou commitment. Compromise = ceder um pouco.

questions.prompt: My _____ is full until the fifteenth.
questions.explanation: “Schedule” is your agenda; it is also a verb.

questions.prompt: I have an _____ with the dentist at four.
questions.explanation: You HAVE an appointment and you MAKE one — never “mark” it.

questions.prompt: Há um atraso de dois dias na entrega.
questions.answer: There is a two-day delay in the delivery.|There's a two-day delay in the delivery.

questions.prompt: We have a _____ call every Monday.
questions.explanation: “Weekly” = once a week; “daily”, “monthly” follow the same pattern.

questions.prompt: You check your email two times a day. You check it…
questions.explanation: “A” here means “per”: twice a day, three times a week.
“Due on” a day, “due in” two weeks.

questions.prompt: You want the other person to choose the time. You ask:
I need more _____ before the meeting.
questions.explanation: “Data” is normally uncountable in everyday English: more data, not more datas.

questions.prompt: Nobody was happy, but both sides gave up something. They reached a…
questions.explanation: “Compromise” is a middle-ground deal. The Portuguese “compromisso” is “appointment” or “commitment”.
